body:
### Describe the bug

Build & run repro:

```console
  $ cythonize -i crash_repro.pyx                                                                                                                                                                                     
  $ python -c "import crash_repro; crash_repro.trigger()"                                                                                                                                                            
```

Actual (CPython 3.14.4, release build):

```
  Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Current thread's C stack trace (most recent call first):                                                                                                                                                           
    Binary file "python", at PyTraceBack_Here+0x31                                                                                                                                                                   
    Binary file ".../crash_repro...so", at +0x6814      # __Pyx_AddTraceback                                                                                                                                         
    Binary file ".../crash_repro...so", at +0x6d89      # trigger() error path                                                                                                                                       
    Binary file "python", at PyObject_Vectorcall+0x33                                                                                                                                                                
    ...                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Extension modules: crash_repro (total: 1)                                                                                                                                                                          
```

exit=139. On macOS the same crash shows EXC\_BAD\_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) … KERN\_INVALID\_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000028.

### Root cause

Cython emits \_\_Pyx\_AddTraceback(...) at error labels, which ends in PyTraceBack\_Here(py\_frame) assuming a raised exception is set. When an except-sentinel cdef function returns its sentinel without setting one,

the error label is reached with tstate->current\_exception == NULL. On CPython ≥ 3.12, PyTraceBack\_Here (https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.4/Python/traceback.c#L322-L327) does:

```c
  PyObject *exc = PyErr_GetRaisedException();   // NULL when nothing is set                                                                                                                                          
  assert(PyExceptionInstance_Check(exc));       // compiled out in release builds                                                                                                                                    
  PyObject *tb = PyException_GetTraceback(exc);  // reads exc->traceback                                                                                                                                             
```

traceback is the 4th pointer in PyException\_HEAD (https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.4/Include/cpython/pyerrors.h#L8-L11) → offset 0x28. So PyException\_GetTraceback(NULL) reads address 0x28 → SIGSEGV

(matches the fault address exactly). In a debug build the assert fires instead, confirming the invariant.

### Affected versions (source-confirmed)

≤ 3.11 (3.11.9 (https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.11.9/Python/traceback.c#L272-L275))  │ PyErr\_Fetch(...) — NULL-tolerant │ safe  │
3.12 (3.12.0 (https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.0/Python/traceback.c#L243-L246)) / 3.13 / 3.14 │ PyErr\_GetRaisedException() + unconditional deref │ segfault │

Runtime-verified crash on CPython 3.14.4; 3.12/3.13 have the identical vulnerable code path (source inference — not run here). Reproduced with Cython 3.2.8, 3.2.9, and 3.3.0a1 (the generated \_\_Pyx\_AddTraceback is unchanged across them).

### Suggested fix

Guard the call in Cython's \_\_Pyx\_AddTraceback (Cython/Utility/Exceptions.c) so PyTraceBack\_Here only runs when an exception is actually set, e.g. if (\_\_Pyx\_PyErr\_Occurred()) PyTraceBack\_Here(py\_frame);. (Related to #4722, which fixed exception-clobbering in \_\_Pyx\_AddTraceback; this is the ≥3.12 NULL-exception case.) Separately, CPython's public PyTraceBack\_Here arguably shouldn't crash on a missing exception.

### Real-world impact

This is the root cause of the segfault in [aiohttp](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/issues/13203) (brotli decode on CPython 3.14): a decode error path reaches \_\_Pyx\_AddTraceback in the compiled \_http\_parser with no live exception, and crashes at the same PyTraceBack\_Here+0x31.

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```cython
  # cython: language_level=3                                                                                                                                                                                         
  cdef int _returns_sentinel(int x) except -1:                                                                                                                                                                       
      # `except -1` declares -1 as the *unambiguous* error sentinel, so Cython                                                                                                                                       
      # omits the PyErr_Occurred() check at the call site. Returning the sentinel                                                                                                                                    
      # (x == -1) makes the caller take its error path with NO exception set.                                                                                                                                        
      return x                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  def trigger():                                                                                                                                                                                                     
      _returns_sentinel(-1)           
```


### Expected behaviour

a clean Python-level error (historically a SystemError), never an interpreter segfault.

### OS

_No response_

### Python version

3.12+

### Cython version

3.2.8, 3.2.9, and 3.3.0a1 confirmed

### Additional context

<details>
<summary>Prepared patch with AI help. We're not 100% confident if it's correct or not, so leaving this here if someone wants to use it.</summary>

```diff
index b0755b3d9..1bfbf037e 100644
--- a/CHANGES.rst
+++ b/CHANGES.rst
@@ -72,6 +72,12 @@ Features added
 Bugs fixed
 ----------
 
+* A ``cdef`` function that returned its exception sentinel value without setting
+  an exception (e.g. ``cdef int f() except -1: return -1``) crashed in CPython 3.12+
+  while building the traceback for the error.  It now propagates CPython's
+  ``SystemError`` instead, as it did in earlier CPython versions.
+  Reported by Sam Bull.
+
 * Several issues with ``.close()`` or ``.throw()`` of Async generator asend/athrow
   objects were resolved, following fixes in CPython.
   (Github issue :issue:`7777`)
diff --git a/Cython/Utility/Exceptions.c b/Cython/Utility/Exceptions.c
index 5c49d94b6..2dbe5e489 100644
--- a/Cython/Utility/Exceptions.c
+++ b/Cython/Utility/Exceptions.c
@@ -878,6 +878,10 @@ static void __Pyx_AddTraceback(const char *funcname, int c_line,
     PyObject *replace = NULL, *getframe = NULL, *frame = NULL;
     PyObject *exc_type, *exc_value, *exc_traceback;
     int success = 0;
+    // If no exception is set, there is nothing to attach a traceback to.
+    // Calling PyTraceBack_Here() without a current exception crashes in
+    // CPython 3.12+ and corrupted the exception state in earlier versions.
+    if (unlikely(!PyErr_Occurred())) return;
     if (c_line) {
         c_line = __Pyx_CLineForTraceback(__Pyx_PyThreadState_Current, c_line);
     }
@@ -975,6 +979,19 @@ static void __Pyx_AddTraceback(const char *funcname, int c_line,
     PyThreadState *tstate = __Pyx_PyThreadState_Current;
     PyObject *ptype, *pvalue, *ptraceback;
 
+    // If no exception is set, there is nothing to attach a traceback to.
+    // Calling PyTraceBack_Here() without a current exception crashes in
+    // CPython 3.12+ and corrupted the exception state in earlier versions.
+#if CYTHON_FAST_THREAD_STATE
+  #if PY_VERSION_HEX >= 0x030C00A6
+    if (unlikely(!tstate->current_exception)) return;
+  #else
+    if (unlikely(!tstate->curexc_type)) return;
+  #endif
+#else
+    if (unlikely(!PyErr_Occurred())) return;
+#endif
+
     if (c_line) {
         c_line = __Pyx_CLineForTraceback(tstate, c_line);
     }
diff --git a/tests/run/add_traceback_no_exception.pyx b/tests/run/add_traceback_no_exception.pyx
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..b75ee64b7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/run/add_traceback_no_exception.pyx
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+# mode: run
+# tag: traceback
+
+import platform
+import sys
+
+
+cdef int return_sentinel_without_exception(int x) except -1:
+    # Deliberate user bug: returns the exception sentinel value (-1)
+    # without setting an exception when x == -1.  This must not crash:
+    # __Pyx_AddTraceback() used to call PyTraceBack_Here() with no
+    # exception set, which segfaults in CPython 3.12+.
+    # See https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/issues/13203
+    return x
+
+
+def call_sentinel(x):
+    return return_sentinel_without_exception(x)
+
+
+def test_ok_value():
+    """
+    >>> test_ok_value()
+    2
+    """
+    return call_sentinel(2)
+
+
+# Returning NULL from a def function without setting an exception triggers
+# CPython's function result check: a SystemError in release builds, but a
+# hard Py_FatalError abort in Py_DEBUG builds.  PyPy's behaviour at that
+# boundary differs as well.  Only doctest the well-defined CPython
+# release-build outcome.
+if platform.python_implementation() == 'CPython' and not hasattr(sys, 'gettotalrefcount'):
+    __doc__ = """
+    >>> try:
+    ...     call_sentinel(-1)
+    ... except SystemError:
+    ...     print("SystemError")
+    SystemError
+
+    The exception state must be intact afterwards:
+
+    >>> try:
+    ...     call_sentinel(-1)
+    ... except SystemError:
+    ...     pass
+    >>> raise ValueError("still works")
+    Traceback (most recent call last):
+    ValueError: still works
+    """```
```
</details>

comment_data.body:
I think this is (mostly) a user error. As you note in the code to reproduce.

```
      # `except -1` declares -1 as the *unambiguous* error sentinel, so Cython                                                                                                                                       
      # omits the PyErr_Occurred() check at the call site. Returning the sentinel                                                                                                                                    
      # (x == -1) makes the caller take its error path with NO exception set.   
```

Given that it is a slow error handling path, it probably doesn't cost us a huge amount to add a check there so it might be worth doing for the sake of better diagnostics.

I suspect this isn't the only way to crash it with misleading exception specifications though.

title: [BUG] Py 3.12+ Segfault in __Pyx_AddTraceback → PyTraceBack_Here when an error path is reached with no exception set
